headline: Finding objects with a phone
intro: AR Navigator is a mobile prototype that points toward a selected object with an arrow, spatial sound, and vibration. I proposed the idea for people with vision impairments and built it with my course team in Unity.
context: University of Michigan · XR course project · November–December 2022
role: I came up with the concept, helped develop it in Unity and C#, and revised the interaction with the team through weekly peer playtests.

question.title: Choosing what to find
question.text: The app offers two ways to set a target: select a common object detected by the camera, or add a labelled reference image from the photo library. Both modes use the same types of directional cues.

steps.title: Select a target
steps.text: The phone runs YOLOv3-tiny to detect common objects and AR Foundation to track image references. Users can select a target or cycle through the available ones.

steps.title: Turn toward it
steps.text: An arrow and spatial ping indicate direction. The phone vibrates when it lines up with the target.

steps.title: Control the search
steps.text: Spoken labels and accessibility support help users operate the controls and stop guidance when they're finished.

gallery.alt: Diagram of object detection and image references converging into one target-selection and guidance workflow.
gallery.caption: Object detection searches for categories the model recognizes. Image tracking uses a specific visual reference supplied by the user.

finding.title: The two modes were confusing in playtests
finding.text: Peer testers could use the audio and vibration, but the difference between the modes wasn't clear. We focused on connecting the two search flows and revising the interface, and set aside a partially developed radar map.

details: The browser demo recreates the interaction with generated scenery and detections. The linked team trailer shows the original mobile application.
We used peer playtests to improve the design. We haven't established how well the prototype works for people with vision impairments.
credits: A University of Michigan student team project, built in Unity with AR Foundation, Barracuda, and Apple accessibility support.
The diagrams were created for this portfolio.
